Q2: Tower Defense (TD) Games; Surveillance / Management Games
Q11: When two or three rooms came under attack at the same time I found it hard to decide which barrier to repair first. The sidebar helps, but I kept tunnel-visioning on the room I was already in and losing track of the others until the damage alert had already gone off.
Q12: The turret upgrade cost was shown as a single lump sum, so I wasn't sure whether it was per-room or a one-time global unlock. I held off buying it for two waves because I was afraid of wasting Power.
Q13: The audio cue for a room losing Power was easy to miss while I was focused on another camera. A persistent 'low power' icon on the room itself would have helped more than the sound.
Q14: Yes, I picked it up around Wave 4. It completely reframed the enemies for me - they stopped being 'monsters to shoot' and became people trying to contain me, which made defending feel morally heavier. I loved it and wish the hints had started even earlier.
Q15: Add a persistent minimap or a status strip that shows all four rooms (barrier health, Power, turret status) at a glance, so I never have to tab away just to check.
Q16: A turret occasionally kept firing at an already-destroyed enemy for a second or two, and one camera switch caused a brief hitch. Nothing game-breaking.

Q11: There are no global hotkeys for switching cameras, so everything has to go through mouse clicks. Coming from RTS games I kept reaching for number keys to jump between rooms, and the forced clicking slowed me down a lot during Wave 4 and 5.
Q12: I wasn't sure for a while whether Power was shared across all rooms or tracked per room. It only became obvious when I spent everything on one side and suddenly had nothing left elsewhere. A clearer 'shared pool' indicator would fix it.
Q13: Barrier health bars were too subtle. I missed a door that was nearly dead until it broke, because the damage readout didn't stand out from the rest of the UI.
Q14: I caught the twist, but only in the Wave 4 dialogue. I understood that I'm the AI and the 'enemies' are a containment team, and it made me question who the aggressor really is. I just wish it had landed earlier so it could motivate the first few waves.
Q15: Add hotkeys for camera switching and a command queue so you can issue an action to a room you aren't currently viewing - it would make the pressure feel like skill instead of click speed.
Q16: Frame drops on Wave 5 once there were a lot of enemies on screen, and one full crash right at the start of Wave 5 that forced me to replay it.

Q11: Juggling the Power dial while flipping between cameras was the worst part. I could only really watch one room at a time, so I always felt like I was abandoning the other three and one of them would get hit the moment I looked away.
Q12: Yes - early on I didn't understand that Power is allocated, not consumed. I dumped everything into one turret and thought I had soft-locked myself until I figured out the allocation model. A short tutorial loop would have saved me a lot of frustration.
Q13: The 'room unsafe' state didn't blink or change color aggressively enough. A couple of times a room was no longer safe and I only noticed because I happened to glance at it.
Q14: I understood it. The reveal made the whole session feel much heavier - I stopped thinking of them as 'enemies' and started thinking of myself as the thing they were trying to shut down. It actually changed how I wanted to play, which I liked.
Q15: Slow down the early waves and add a proper tutorial for the Power system. The atmosphere is great but I spent the first two waves fighting the controls instead of learning them.
Q16: Some audio stuttering when a lot of enemies spawned at once, but no crashes or hard bugs.

Q11: Everything felt like it demanded my attention at the same time, and I had no idea what to prioritize first. I'd panic, click around randomly, and then realize I'd spent the whole wave doing nothing useful.
Q12: Yes. I couldn't tell the difference between 'Power to activate a device' and 'Power to buy an upgrade'. I assumed buying an upgrade permanently spent from the same pool, so I was way too conservative with my Power.
Q13: I kept missing when a turret was destroyed because there was no clear popup or callout. The icon just silently vanished from the room.
Q14: The twist genuinely surprised me - I had not guessed it at all. It recontextualized why I was defending, and it made me much more engaged with the story for the later waves.
Q15: Add a real onboarding tutorial with tooltips on hover. I spent too much time guessing what the icons meant, and a new player shouldn't have to.
Q16: I had to restart once because the UI got stuck and stopped responding to camera clicks. Recovering was fine after the restart.

Q11: The difficulty wall hit me almost immediately. I couldn't keep four rooms alive with the limited Power I had, and I got steamrolled on Wave 2 and 3 repeatedly. It didn't feel like a skill issue - it felt like I wasn't given the tools to respond.
Q12: Yes - upgrade costs felt arbitrary. I couldn't tell which upgrades were worth buying or what they actually did, so I ended up spending Power on things that didn't help me survive.
Q13: Nearly everything blended together. All the alerts were the same shade of red, so I couldn't tell a damaged barrier from a lost turret from a low-Power warning at a glance.
Q14: I never reached the twist during my playthrough, so I'm answering based on what I read in the survey description. From that, I understand the player is the AI and the enemies are a containment team, which is a cool idea - but I didn't get far enough to experience it.
Q15: Rebalance the early waves and make the alerts visually distinct. Right now the difficulty curve is so steep that I couldn't even reach the content the survey cares about most.
Q16: Yes, one hard lock when I switched cameras rapidly back and forth - the game froze and I had to force quit.
